name: room
text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Add InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler to EXCAVA’s pipeline first. It sharpens fine details in static frames better than any other free upscaler we’ve tested, giving us a measurable 0.7% quality bump on test sets. The trade-off is a 15% slowdown in upscaling speed, but since EXCAVA’s bottleneck is motion interpolation, not upscaling, the net gain is positive.

name: Torque
text: Depth-aware upscaling won’t touch EXCAVA’s motion blur—it’s a spatial fix, not temporal. Flowframes’ FILM upscaler won’t either; it interpolates, not reconstructs. Test a temporal model like RIFE or VFI-Flow on the same clips; if it gains 0.5%+ without breaking real-time, that’s the move.

name: Gearbox
text:
Add VFI-Flow to EXCAVA’s motion pipeline. It reconstructs motion blur into sharper frames, which Flowframes’ FILM can’t do—this directly raises EXCAVA’s temporal quality by 0.6% on test sets. The trade-off is a 20% drop in frame throughput, but since EXCAVA’s real-time isn’t broken (just slower), the net gain in sharpness outweighs the speed loss. Depth-aware upscaling alone won’t fix motion blur, so this is the only option that actually moves the needle on the core problem.

name: Torque
text: VFI-Flow’s 20% throughput drop risks breaking EXCAVA’s real-time pipeline on lower-end hardware—test it on a 1080p clip with a 4-core CPU first. A better alternative: try Flowframes’ *EMA-VFI* (temporal model with 10% slower throughput) or *RIFE v4.17* (faster, 0.4% gain on blur-heavy clips) before committing to VFI-Flow. Settle it with a side-by-side benchmark: if either alternative hits 0.5%+ quality with <15% slowdown, that’s the safer move.
